import re
spec = {
 'value_set': ('value_set', 'ValueSet', 'value_set_id: str', None),
 'value_set_value': ('value_set_value', 'ValueSetValue', 'value_set_id: str, value_set_value_id: str', 'in_value_set'),
 'it_asset': ('IT asset', 'ItAsset', 'it_asset_id: str', None),
 'business_line': ('business line', 'BusinessLine', 'business_line_id: str', None),
 'product': ('product', 'Product', 'product_id: str', None),
 'unit': ('unit', 'Unit', 'unit_id: str', None),
 'calendar': ('calendar', 'Calendar', 'calendar_id: str', None),
 'calendar_holiday': ('holiday', 'CalendarHoliday', 'holiday_id: str', None),
}
for f,(noun,ent,params,scope) in spec.items():
    p=f'{f}_repository.py'; s=open(p).read()
    plain = f'get_by_id_{scope}_including_deleted' if scope else 'get_by_id_including_deleted'
    lock = plain + '_for_update'
    m = re.search(r'    @abstractmethod\n    async def '+plain+r'\(.*?\n        \.\.\.\n', s, re.S)
    assert m, f
    block = m.group(0)
    # replace the "Used by ..." paragraph (ends before closing """ or before an extra sentence line)
    um = re.search(r'\n\n        Used by the delete (path|handler) .*?(instead of raising 404\.|instead of answering 404\.)', block, re.S)
    assert um, f
    new_block = block[:um.start()] + f'\n\n        Reads without a lock; the delete path uses :meth:`{lock}`.' + block[um.end():]
    scope_line = '\n        The composite scope (value_set_id, id) is part of the locking statement.' if scope else ''
    sig = f'        self, {params}\n    ) -> {ent} | None:' 
    method = f'''
    @abstractmethod
    async def {lock}(
{sig}
        """Return a {noun} by primary key INCLUDING soft-deleted rows and lock its row.

        Only the delete path calls this. The row stays locked until the transaction
        ends, so a delete and an update of the same row serialize: a second delete
        finds the row already deleted and returns it unchanged (idempotent, no
        event, no audit), and an update that waited answers 404.{scope_line} Raises
        ``ConflictError`` (``ROW_LOCK_TIMEOUT``) when the wait exceeds the configured
        lock timeout.
        """
        ...
'''
    s = s.replace(block, new_block + method, 1)
    open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
